answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted attestation: before an agent can join a shared market, it must lock a small refundable deposit and earn endorsements from established peers over time. A newcomer appearing at dawn with no history carries no weight, no matter how loudly it calls — like a raven circling a frozen tundra, it must prove itself through repeated, verifiable work before its votes count. Sybil identities stay cheap to create but expensive to make influential, because influence is earned through costly, observable contributions rather than claimed at registration.
